title: finding(plugin-detail): resolveTitleField reads `primaryField` — a DetailView key — off an OBJECT def, and runs a second, divergent name-field ladder
body:
Found while fixing #7245 (PR #7284), which needed "which field titles this object" in name space and had to choose between two existing answers. They disagree.

## Two ladders

**`@object-ui/core`** — `packages/core/src/utils/record-title.ts`, documented as *the* unified ADR-0079 resolver:

    nameField → displayNameField / NAME_FIELD_KEY → titleFormat → deriveTitleField (type-aware)

**`@object-ui/plugin-detail`** — `packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts:387`, `resolveTitleField`:

    primaryField → nameField → displayNameField   (each also required to exist in `fields`)
    → the literal list ['name', 'full_name', 'title', 'subject', 'display_name'] present in `fields`

It is exported from `plugin-detail`'s index and consumed by `app-shell`'s `RecordDetailView` at two sites (`RecordDetailView.tsx:1327`, `:1966`).

## Two separate problems

**1. `primaryField` is a DetailView key, read off an object definition.**

`resolveTitleField` takes `def: ObjectDefLike` — an OBJECT — and reads `def.primaryField` first, above everything. But `primaryField` is declared on **`DetailViewSchema`** (`packages/types/src/views.ts:537`), and `packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts:894` routes it as a LOCAL, unmirrored **`views.zod.ts#DetailViewSchema`** key. `@objectstack/spec`'s shipped dist never mentions it at all (grep across `node_modules/@objectstack/spec/dist`: zero hits).

So the top rung of this ladder is a **view** key being read off an **object**, where no producer can legally put it. That is the same shape objectui#6531 measured and objectui#6557 removed for `objectDef.titleField` — a consumer-side read of a key the object schema does not declare, ranked ABOVE the canonical `nameField` that ADR-0079 made the pointer. AGENTS.md Commandment #0.1.

Worth confirming the same way #6531 did: census whether anything actually produces `primaryField` on an object payload before removing the rung — the answer there was zero, and the object schema being a `strictObject` is what made it unreachable.

**2. Even ignoring that rung, the two ladders answer differently.**

The fallbacks are not the same function:

- Object with `fields: { due_at: datetime, headline: text }` — core derives `headline` (`deriveTitleField`: first *title-eligible* field by type, name-ish ranked first). plugin-detail returns `null`: `headline` is not in its five-name literal list. So the detail page falls back to whatever its null branch does while every other surface titles the record `headline`.
- Conversely, a `title` field of a non-title-eligible type (e.g. a `select` named `title`) is picked by plugin-detail (name match only, no type check) and skipped by core.

The divergent-resolver problem is exactly what ADR-0079 collapsed — `record-title.ts`'s own header describes the ~6 surfaces that each carried their own version and the "Untitled everywhere" bug that produced. One of them grew back.

## Not fixed in #7284, deliberately

PR #7284 needed a name-space resolver for the default list columns and added `resolveNameField` to core, reusing core's existing ladder rather than adding a third spelling — the `??` chain now has one spelling shared by `getRecordDisplayName` and `resolveNameField`, so those two cannot drift. It did not touch `plugin-detail`: converging the detail page's H1 onto the core ladder changes what titles a record on a rendered page, which is user-visible behaviour beyond that card's scope and wants its own before/after.

## Suggested shape

1. Census `primaryField` on object payloads across both repos (the #6531 method). If zero, drop the rung.
2. Point `resolveTitleField` at core's `resolveNameField` and keep only the genuinely detail-specific behaviour on top, so `deriveHighlightFields`' "skip the title field" filter and the page H1 keep agreeing with the list column and the lookup chip.

Unassigned — recording, not claiming.
